extracted.intended_audience: readers of The A.V. Club / viewers interested in television criticism and comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance for reviewing or producing a talk-show parody TV series, focusing on tone, construction of bits, use of guests, self-awareness, and the balance between format constraints and comic lunacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificiality — be the most artificial riff on an artificial format
rubrics_metrics.description: If the show is going to be an artificial riff on a format where everything is artificial, it ought to be the most artificial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal devices that call attention to artifice (e.g., live-action-cartoon motif, green-screen exposure) so the show itself foregrounds its constructedness; season finales or signature episodes can serve as declarations of this intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical targets are ideas, not people
rubrics_metrics.description: Its satirical targets are ideas, not people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim satire at the absurdity of showbiz and media culture rather than humiliating guests or mocking fan communities; the joke should not be at a guest's expense and should avoid mean-spirited potshots (e.g., avoid punching down at rabid fans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampoon from a place of knowledge; construct clever bits
rubrics_metrics.description: Gags ... aren’t 'everything sucks' drive-by hits. They’re cleverly constructed bits of sketch comedy, ones that demonstrate a knowledge of their subjects that simultaneously exposes the seams of television production—and the seams of Comedy Bang! Bang! itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write sketches that show familiarity with the formats or genres being parodied (examples: 'Cop Swap', hidden-camera 'Date-Zaster', Jimmy Pardo-hosted game show). Avoid shallow, generic put-downs; prefer bits that reveal specific production or genre mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose the seams — self-aware production choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The show grants itself an increased number of opportunities to show those seams, pausing to let a reaction linger or blocking a shot in order to catch the edges of the set walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editing, blocking, and performance pacing to intentionally reveal artifice (lingering reactions, visible set edges) as a comedic tactic; self-referential exposure reinforces the parody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: put-on sincerity combined with a sneer of condescension
rubrics_metrics.description: Aukerman’s put-on smile never hides a sneer of condescension, the sign of a unique fascination and amusement with the plastic nature of show business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a balance between feigned earnestness and an undercurrent of knowing irony; warmth in the performance helps keep faux sincerity from becoming purely contemptuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tightly controlled chaos and wholehearted commitment to silliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Tightly controlled chaos still reigns on Comedy Bang! Bang!, but the show finds new facets of itself ... by easing up enough to, say, let Paul F. Tompkins call attention to the phoniness of his Garry Marshall dye job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an overall editorial control so the madness reads as intentional rather than sloppy; let silliness be explored from many angles while preserving structural discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when to relent — loosen format constraints to allow lunacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The next steps for the show might be to relent even further, to the point where it can let some of the more rigid aspects of the talk-show format fall away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to suspend or discard strict format conventions when doing so enables wilder, more original comedy; beware of episodes that remain tied too tightly to set or conceit (example: musical extravaganza that 'falls short of total lunacy' because it's constrained by Aukerman’s mock living room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful and effective use of guests and guest personas
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when a guest seems caught off-guard ... the joke is never at their expense. The point is to laugh at the absurdity of showbiz, never to damn it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate guests in ways that highlight the parody without embarrassing or undermining them; use guest strengths (e.g., Paul Reubens as Pee-wee, Gillian Jacobs episode) to play with expectations and create meta-humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical cultural/media satire — critique viewing habits and TV culture
rubrics_metrics.description: The episode puckishly nullifies what’s happening in the present—critiquing viewers’ Internet-age habit of staying one step ahead of their favorite shows ... exaggerating the current TV culture's search for the latest and greatest 'best show ever.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build episodes that comment on contemporary media practices (spoiler culture, hype cycles, hashtag-obsessed fandom) using exaggerated in-show analogues (e.g., a hashtag-spouting host) to frame the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrow strengths from predecessor formats (podcast roots) to find new facets
rubrics_metrics.description: The show finds new facets of itself (ones borrowed from its podcast predecessor) by easing up enough to, say, let Paul F. Tompkins call attention to the phoniness of his Garry Marshall dye job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage elements from related or antecedent formats (podcast spontaneity, improv sensibilities) to enrich television iterations; allow the looseness of those forms to inform on-screen moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance choices and character work should enhance the parody
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Bobby Moynihan’s performance as 'stabby' orphan child Fourvel ('It’s like Fievel but one less') or Aukerman’s deadpan reading of the ad copy for the fictional Comedy Bang! Bang! Cruise ('The bottom of the boat keeps hitting fish').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage performers to commit to specific, vivid character choices and delivery (deadpan reads, exaggerated child characters, faux-ad copy) that clarify the joke and deepen the parody.
